doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

chapter: Teaching, tradition and the banjo's roots
title: A planned Africa trip to trace the banjo's origins
summary: Next year Fleck will spend four to six weeks in West and East Africa recording an album and documentary footage. The trip would be impossible in a regular Flecktones year.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Because that’s one of the things that I’m really interested in doing.

West Africa will be a big part of it but also East Africa just because I have a friend who does tours over there who knows a lot of musicians in Uganda and Tanzania. So that’s going to be an interesting thing, which would have been hard to do in a regular Flecktone year because, you know, six weeks of not being available and then the time I’ll need to recover. Six weeks is a long time for a band to be off when they’re all trying to make a living. But for this year I’m going to be doing different things.
